text.p: These are the leading stories of Albania's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Seven members of the new Socialist government will fly to Rome on Wednesday to attend a meeting of European donors for Albania.
- The Albanian government delegation in Rome will request a 50 million dollar credit to help stabilise the lek currency, which has suffered steep devaluation since January.
- Restoring law and order, passing a constitution and getting the economy back on track are the three main pillars of the Socialist government programme.
- Albania's parliamentary speaker Skender Gjinushi said a new constitution will first be approved by parliament and later submitted to a referendum.
- Prime Minister Fatos Nano said his government would compensate losses in collapsed pyramid investment schemes as much as possible.
- The opposition Democratic Party has not returned to parliament although the stages it said it would boycott, the election of the president and prime minister, have now been dealt with.
- Transport and construction specialists have protested over the merging of their sectors under one ministry, saying such a structure exists only in Bosnia-Herzegovina.
- The Finance Ministry plans to start a crackdown on companies that import cigarettes illegally.
- Prec Zogaj, a journalist and member of the centre-right Democratic Alliance Party, will become political councillor to President Rexhep Mejdani.

- Prime Minister Fatos Nano said his government would try to find the money lost in pyramid schemes even if the funds are deposited abroad and it would start checking immediately the schemes' ability to pay back creditors.
- Shooting and chaos prevailed in the southern anarchic town of Vlore immediately after Italian soldiers left the town, despite appeals by town authorities to postpone their departure.
- Interior Minister Neritan Ceka has removed heads of departments and all police station chiefs but one in Tirana, replacing them with policemen with at least ten years' work experience.
